expected_pattern: XGBoost was expected to improve intermittent demand after its strong inner-validation result in Fold 1.
observed_pattern: Fold 1 intermittent WRMSSE increased from 0.994666 to 1.351116, a deterioration of 35.8361%.
why_surprising: The inner-validation WRMSSE was 0.731678 and selected 1,250 rounds, but this performance did not transfer to the following outer-test period.
possible_non_causal_explanation: The relationship between recent history, covariates and sparse demand may have changed between the validation and test windows.
planned_follow_up: Inspect feature ablation and SHAP results for intermittent demand. Do not retune using Fold 1 outer-test information.
status: Open for Step 17 and SHAP analysis

expected_pattern: Lower bottom-level errors were expected to coincide with a lower overall WRMSSE.
observed_pattern: Fold 1 intermittent MAE improved by 19.8228%, while WRMSSE deteriorated by 35.8361%.
why_surprising: The two metrics gave opposite conclusions for the same model and test period.
possible_non_causal_explanation: WRMSSE assigns dollar-sales weights and evaluates all 12 hierarchy levels, while bottom-level MAE treats individual errors differently.
planned_follow_up: Retain both results and examine which hierarchy levels produced the WRMSSE deterioration.

expected_pattern: Lumpy demand was expected to be difficult, but the model was expected to perform similarly across folds.
observed_pattern: Lumpy XGBoost improved WRMSSE in Folds 2–5 but deteriorated by 14.9296% in Fold 1.
why_surprising: The Fold 1 loss contrasted with improvements of 7.8800%, 27.0139%, 27.3392% and 7.8310% in the remaining folds.
possible_non_causal_explanation: The first outer-test period may contain a different combination of sparse demand events and aggregation effects.
planned_follow_up: Compare Fold 1 with later lumpy folds during ablation and SHAP analysis.
status: Open for Step 17 and SHAP analysis

expected_pattern: Mean fold-specific improvement and improvement from mean WRMSSE scores were expected to have the same sign.
observed_pattern: For intermittent demand, improvement from the mean scores was +0.5025%, while the arithmetic mean of fold percentages was -0.9984%.
why_surprising: The same five folds produced two differently signed summary percentages.
possible_non_causal_explanation: Percentage changes use different denominators in each fold. Averaging those percentages is not equivalent to calculating a percentage from the two mean WRMSSE values.
planned_follow_up: Report the improvement from mean scores as the main summary and also provide fold wins, median change and the Fold 1 exception.

expected_pattern: A similar number of boosting rounds was expected across adjacent folds.
observed_pattern: Selected rounds varied from 150 to 1,250. Intermittent demand changed from 1,250 rounds in Fold 1 to 160 rounds in Fold 2.
why_surprising: The preferred model size changed sharply despite using the same algorithm and feature set.
possible_non_causal_explanation: Each inner-validation period presented a different forecast origin and temporal demand pattern.
planned_follow_up: Retain fold-specific selection and report the variation as evidence of temporal instability, not as proof of demand complexity.

expected_pattern: Improvements at detailed hierarchy levels were expected to carry through to aggregated levels.
observed_pattern: Intermittent and lumpy demand showed strong mean gains at item and item-store levels, but weaker or negative results at total, state and category levels.
why_surprising: Aggregation did not consistently strengthen the individual-series improvements.
possible_non_causal_explanation: Small directionally related errors can accumulate when forecasts are aggregated.
planned_follow_up: Use hierarchy-level ablation results to determine whether particular feature groups contribute to aggregate forecast bias.
